name: Observer
intent: Let one object notify many others when its state changes, without knowing who they are.
scenario: A news channel publishes headlines. Email and SMS subscribers want each one, and can join or leave at any time.
problem: A news channel must tell other parts of the system when a headline is published. If the channel calls each recipient directly, it has to know every recipient class. Every new way of being notified means editing the channel.
solution: The channel (the subject) keeps a list of observers behind a tiny interface. It calls update() on each one when something happens. Observers register and unregister themselves, so the channel never learns what they do.
pain: NewsChannel creates and calls EmailSender and SmsSender directly
Adding push notifications means editing NewsChannel
NewsChannel cannot be tested without real senders
benefits: NewsChannel only knows the Observer interface
New subscriber types need zero changes to the channel
Subscribers can join and leave while the program runs
Tests can subscribe a simple fake
whenToUse: A change in one object must trigger updates in an unknown or changing set of others
You want loose coupling between the source of events and the reactions
UI updates, event buses, live data feeds, plugin hooks
whenNotToUse: There is exactly one fixed listener: call it directly
Order of notifications matters and must be guaranteed
You need request/response semantics rather than fire-and-forget
pitfalls: Memory leaks: forgetting to unsubscribe keeps observers alive
Update storms: observers that trigger more updates can loop
An observer that throws can stop the rest from being notified unless you guard each call
Hidden control flow makes debugging harder than a direct call

roles.label: Subject
roles.description: Holds state of interest and the list of observers; notifies them.

roles.label: Observer
roles.description: Interface with an update() method that subjects call.

roles.label: Concrete Observer
roles.description: A real reaction: send an email, send an SMS, redraw a chart.

quiz.question: A dashboard widget subscribes to a live price feed when it opens. Users open and close widgets all day, but the code never unsubscribes. After a few hours memory has grown and closed widgets still receive updates. What is the fix?
options: Slow the feed to one update per second, so the closed widgets have less work to do
Clear the feed's whole observer list every minute and let the open widgets register again
Call the garbage collector on a timer, since closed widgets are no longer visible to users
Unsubscribe each widget from the feed when it closes, so the feed drops its reference
quiz.explanation: The subject's list holds a reference to every observer, so closed widgets cannot be freed and keep reacting. They must unregister when they close. Slowing the feed or forcing collection does not release objects that are still referenced.

quiz.question: A subject notifies 3 observers in a loop. The first observer throws an exception on one event, and the other two never hear about it. What is the best fix?
options: Wrap the whole notification loop in one try block and log whatever it catches
Make notification run in reverse order, so the failing observer cannot block its neighbours
Guard each observer call separately so a failure is logged and the loop continues
Reorder the observers so that the one that fails most often is always called last
quiz.explanation: One bad observer should not hide events from the others, so each call gets its own guard. One try around the whole loop still exits at the first failure. Reordering only changes who is affected.

quiz.question: A price subject notifies its observers every time the price is set. A rounding observer reacts to 10.004 by setting the price to 10.00, which notifies everyone again. With a slightly different rule the calls repeat until the stack overflows. What is the best fix?
options: Notify only when the value changed, and keep observers from rewriting the subject
Make notifications asynchronous with a queue, so that the call stack no longer grows
Increase the stack size so that the recursion has room to finish for the values seen
Unsubscribe the rounding observer during every notification and subscribe it again afterwards
quiz.explanation: Skipping notifications for unchanged values lets the cycle settle, and observers should not push changes back into the subject during a notification. A queue only turns the stack overflow into an endless loop. A bigger stack only postpones the failure.
